FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Cordage Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This standard originally published in 1984 has been revised to align it with IS0 1141 : 1990 `Ropes Polyester - Specification', issued by the International Organization for Standardization. Following changes have been incorporated in the revised version: i) Reference number corresponding used as designation of the rope, to nominal diameter in mm has been given and is meant for

ii) Values of minimum breaking load have been modified, and iii) Tolerance on linear density has also been modified. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with,IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding of numerical values (reviseLi)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

MULTIFILAMENT ROPES SPECIFICATION (3-STRAND HAWSER-LAID AND 8-STARND PLAITED) ( First Revision )
1 SCOPE

POLYESTER

This standard specifies requirements for the following types of ropes made out of polyester multifilament yarn: - 3-strand hawser-laid -&strand plaited 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 3871 : 1984 shall apply. 4 ATMOSPHERIC CONDITIONS FOR CONDITIONING AND TESTS The tests may be carried out under prevailing atmospheric conditions. However, in case of dispute, the tests shall be carried out on samples which have been conditioned for 24 hours in a standard atmospheric conditions (65 + 2 percent relative humidity and 27 + 2�C temperature). If practicable, the tests shall be carried out under standard atmospheric conditions. Otherwise the tests shall be carried out as quickly as possible and not later than 15 minutes of removal of the test pieces from the conditioning atmosphere. 5 MANUFACTURE 5.1 Construction
5.1.1 Unless

5.1.3 The number of rope yarns in all the strands shall be same.

5.2 Structure The ropes and their strands shall be continuous, without splice. 5.3 Treatment
The ropes shall be heat stabilized to fix the lay and dimensional stability. This treatment shall ensure dimensional stability so that subsequent shrinkage on use shall be minimal.

5.4 Rope
The twisted rope shall be flexible, well laid and free

from defects in yarn, strand and finish. 6 REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Length of Coil
The length of each coil when tested by the method prescribed in IS 7071 (Part 2) : 1989 shall not be less

than 220 m or as declared. However, if so agreed between the buyer and the seller, the length of coil may be tested under zero tension and the following tolerances shall be applicable on the specified/ declared length :

otherwise specified, hawser-laid ropes shall have `Z' twist, their strands `S' twist and their roping yarns `Z' twist. 5.1.2 Unless otherwise specified, 8-strand plaited ropes shall consist of four pairs of strands, each alternate pair consisting of two `S' twisted and two `Z' twisted strands. 1

NOTE-Any coil which has been shortened by cutting from it, the necessary test sample shall be accepted at its original length and mass as part of the delivery provided that the test sample complies with the specified requirements.

6.2 Mass of the Coil
The

net mass of the coil containing 220 metres of rope including ties and lashing but excluding packing materials shall be as specified in Table 1 and Table 2 for 3-strand hawser-laid and 8-strand plaited ropes respectively.

9 SAMPLING 9.1 Lot The quantity of coils of rope of the same linear density, and type, manufactured under similar conditions and delivered to a buyer against a despatch note shall constitute a lot. 9.2 Sample Size Draw the samples at random, at the rate shown by the following formula to ensure that the samples are as representative as possible of the lot : S = 0.4/N Where S is the number of coils in the sample and N is the size of the lot expressed as the number of coils. When S as calculated is not a whole number, round off the value obtained to give the whole number in accordance with the requirements of IS 2 : 1960. In cases where S is less than 1, draw one coil as sample. 3

9.3 For evaluating the length, linear density, breaking load and pitch, the number of coils selected according to 9.2 shall constitute the test sample. 9.3.1 For evaluating the net mass of the lot, all the coils in the lot shall constitute the test specimen. 9.4 Criteria of Conformity The lot should be declared conforming to the standard if the following conditions are satisfied: a) Length of each coil satisfies the specified/ declared length; b) All the individual test samples tested for breaking load satisfy the specified requirement. However, in case of failure of a test specimen drawn from a coil, another specimen shall be tested from the same coil and the same shall satisfy the specified requirement; and c) Average values of the test results of the lot in respect of other characteristics conform to the specified requirements.

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Zndiun Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. `This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
